definition: To think carefully about a situation so that you can decide what to do about it.
example: Ka-yan spent the night before her birthday taking stock of all she had achieved so far.

definition: To stop doing something harmful that you have done for a long time.
example: Sandy has bitten his nails for years, but he really wants to kick the habit.

definition: To take the opportunity to begin something again.
example: I’m looking forward to making a fresh start this term, training harder, and getting back on the basketball team.

definition: To begin doing a job or activity completely from the beginning.
example: I’m not sure what I’ve done with the designs for my comic book, so I’ll have to start from scratch.

definition: To be more organised
example: Tommy needs to get his act together if he wants to apply for that scholarship – the deadline is next week.

definition: To join an activity or support an opinion that is very fashionable.
example: Clara says she’s always been interested in meditation, but I think she’s just jumping on the bandwagon so she seems cool.

word: Get off on the right foot
definition: To start something positively or successfully.
example: Mark wanted to get off on the right foot in his new role, so he made sure to familiarize himself with all the key tasks in his first week.

definition: Starting fresh without any past mistakes or baggage.
example: After quitting his stressful job, Tom felt like he had a clean slate and could focus on his personal growth and well-being.

definition: To make a big or difficult decision, especially to start something new.
example: After months of hesitation, Kelly decided to take the plunge and start her online store.

definition: To focus on the most important issues and let go of the smaller ones.
example: When planning his resolutions, Leo realized he needed to pick his battles and prioritize achievable goals.

definition: To improve your performance or efforts.
example: To meet his ambitious fitness goals, Jack knew he needed to step up his game and train consistently.

definition: To pause and reconsider a situation.
example: Before setting new goals, the team decided to take a step back and reflect on their past achievements.

definition: To adjust your plans or goals to make them more realistic.
example: Mark realized he needed to recalibrate his expectations and set more achievable goals for the new year.

definition: To enjoy routines and feel comfortable sticking to them.
example: Emily is a creature of habit; she wakes up at the same time every day.

definition: To insist on something being done in a certain way.
example: My boss is a stickler for punctuality and expects everyone to be on time.

definition: It’s difficult to change or stop a habit that has been established over time.
example: Despite his New Year's resolution, he still smokes. Old habits die hard.

definition: To feel trapped in a monotonous routine or unfavorable situation.
example: After working the same job for ten years, she felt stuck in a rut and needed a change.

definition: To continue or uphold a tradition or customary practice.
example: We always keep with tradition and have a family dinner on Sundays.

definition: To stop following a tradition or customary practice.
example: This year, we decided to break with tradition and have a beach holiday instead of a big family gathering.

definition: To act in accordance with the advice or rules you give to others.
example: If you tell your team to work hard, you should practice what you preach and do the same.

definition: To establish a behavior or routine through repetition.
example: It takes time and consistency to form a habit like exercising daily.

definition: To stop doing something harmful or unhealthy.
example: Sarah has been trying to kick her bad habit of biting her nails.

definition: To create a positive routine or behavior.
example: Drinking plenty of water daily is a good habit to develop.

definition: To break free from a monotonous or uninspiring routine.
example: Traveling can help you get out of a rut and bring excitement back into your life.

word: Take it with a grain of salt
definition: To not completely believe something or take it too seriously, especially advice or feedback.
example: He gave me some advice about investing, but I took it with a grain of salt.

definition: To criticize or give constructive feedback to someone.
example: She pulled me up on my presentation, saying I needed more data.

definition: To seriously consider or accept someone's advice or feedback.
example: I took his advice to heart and decided to work on my communication skills.

definition: To face a difficult situation or accept harsh feedback.
example: I didn’t want to hear that feedback, but I had to bite the bullet and listen.

word: In one ear and out the other
definition: When someone doesn’t pay attention to advice or feedback.
example: I gave him some advice, but it just went in one ear and out the other.

word: Give someone a piece of your mind
definition: To give someone frank or blunt advice, usually when you’re upset.
example: I had to give him a piece of my mind after that meeting.

word: Take the bull by the horns
definition: To deal with a difficult situation directly.
example: She took the bull by the horns and gave her manager direct feedback.

word: Hit the nail on the head
definition: To give advice or feedback that is exactly right.
example: You really hit the nail on the head with that suggestion—it’s exactly what we needed.

word: Give someone a pat on the back
definition: To praise someone for their efforts or achievements.
example: She deserved a pat on the back for handling the client so well.
